text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi "will be stained with the blood" of murdered people if government does not move quickly to deal with delays in trying homicide cases, High Court Judge Dyress Kumange warned court officials this week.
- The Chief Resident Magistrate in Malawi's northern region, Charles Mkandawire, on Thursday deplored the persistent mosque fights beween two feuding muslim sects, describing them as shameful.
- A Malawian of Asian origin, carrying about $145,000 in cash, was knifed to death on Wednesday while driving to Lilongwe from Blantyre, police sources said on Thursday.
- Government officials have blamed a Jehova's Witnesses Sect for the country's serious voter apathy experienced in the recent by-elections.
- Police in Lilongwe are holding two men suspected to be behind a spate of car thefts in this administrative capital city, central regional police commissioner George Chirwa said on Thursday.
